content.intro: This lesson develops topic 46 of the supplied curriculum: **Reshaping Arrays with reshape()**. The main starting point is **Specifying new dimensions**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Shape manipulation makes data fit downstream operations, but it must preserve element counts or intentionally change them through joining/splitting. Always check the resulting shape.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Reshaping Arrays with reshape()** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Specifying new dimensions** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.arange(6)
print(a.reshape(2, 3))

Stack adds an axis; concatenate joins along an existing axis.
